title: Indus script: Parpola, 'Study of the Indus Script' (ICES Tokyo 2005) tested against the ICIT-derived and M77 corpora

documents.shelfmark: ICIT-derived corpus, yajnadevam/indus-website population-script.sql (2,543 objects, CISI numbers)

plaintext.source: No bilingual; Parpola's Proto-Dravidian readings of about twenty signs are proposals.

transcription.source: ICIT (Wells and Fuls) as digitised in the indus-website database; glyphs identified by rendering its font
transcription.notes: Fused repeated pairs (e.g. 792 = eye+eye) split back into two signs before counting.

transcription.source: Mahadevan 1977, machine-readable export of indusscript.in (not copied into the folder)
transcription.notes: Counted by m77_checks.py on the external file; 14,153 tokens including 781 unread-sign placeholders.

system.summary: Undeciphered Bronze Age sign system of about 400-600 signs, probably logo-syllabic, written mostly right to left on seals and tablets; language unknown.
system.notes: Diacritics here are the strokes and roofs added to base signs such as the fish (Parpola's 'diacritic additions').

prior_solution.where: No accepted decipherment. Parpola's rebus readings are in print (1994, 2005); the corpus checks of his 2005 claims were computed here.

conditions.human_role: Gave the harappa.com PDF (Parpola's lecture) as the target with /goal; no target-specific intervention.
tools: parpola_checks.py (claim tests, within-line shuffle nulls, bigram surprisal)
align_m77.py (ICIT-to-Mahadevan sign map by text alignment)

solution.what: harappa.com PDF blocked by Cloudflare for plain curl; fetched with a browser user agent. It is Parpola's 2005 lecture, not an inscription.
Looked for machine-readable corpora: mayig CISI (179 texts, too few), indus_decipher (M77, ICIT-derived CSV), yajnadevam indus-website SQL dump with CISI numbers.
Parsed the SQL dump into data/corpus.tsv (2,543 objects, reading order from the direction field) and identified Parpola's signs by rendering the site's font.

Looked up the seals Parpola cites: M-634, M-357, M-1169, M-172, M-57/M-387, M-205, M-478/479, L-11 match his descriptions; K-10 matches only if short and long two-stroke signs are one; seven cited objects absent.
Jar 9.9-11.3% of tokens; jar+jar once in each corpus, on the same unprovenanced round seal (M77 9901 = ICIT 3889); 0 in South Asia against 4.0 expected under within-line shuffle (p about 0.007).
Bigram surprisal of West Asian finds against South Asian texts: round/cylinder seals at the 90th percentile for unusual order; one square seal (Salut) also atypical.

Compound units behind the readings: eye+eye, water+eye, 6+fish, numeral+pot, crab+fish-series significant; 7+fish (1 seal) and fig+fish (1 here) single attestations; crab + plain fish 0; 2+fish (62) and 3+fish (19) unread in the lecture.
Within-line sign repetition is about half of chance at lengths 4-10 (Farmer's observation), consistent with word-level seal legends.

Aligned ICIT and M77 through shared texts (align_m77.py: four repeated tablet sets as seeds, hard EM, 978 lines, 96% sign agreement) and reran the sign claims on M77: same single jar+jar, 7+fish and two fig+fish objects; crab + plain fish below chance, crab + marked fish above.

outcome.notes: Undeciphered script: no bilingual, language unknown. The work tests the corpus evidence behind Parpola's 2005 claims; several confirmed, some readings rest on one or two seals.
